body:
### Summary

I discovered this issue while experimenting with switching pip over to use `uv-build`, as part of research for a blog post. Pip is a pure Python project, but it does make heavy use of vendoring, and thus transitively includes some "data" files (in particular, precompiled stub executables used by `packaging` on Windows). It also keeps vendor licenses with the vendored code in the source tree.

Minimal "narrative" reproducer:

```
$ tree
.
├── dist
├── LICENSE.txt
├── pyproject.toml
└── src
    └── zzz
        ├── __init__.py
        └── _vendor
            ├── LICENSE.txt
            └── thing.bin


5 directories, 5 files
$
$ cat pyproject.toml 
[project]
version = "0.1.0"
name = "zzz"
description = "zzz"
license = "MIT"
license-files = [
  "LICENSE.txt",
  "src/zzz/_vendor/**/LICENSE.txt",
]
[build-system]
requires = ["uv_build>=0.13.1,<0.14"]
build-backend = "uv_build"
$
$ xxd src/zzz/_vendor/thing.bin 
00000000: ff                                       .
$
$ uv build --wheel
Building wheel...
Error: Invalid project metadata

Caused by:
    License file `src/zzz/_vendor/thing.bin` must be UTF-8 encoded
  × Failed to build `/path/to/zzz`
  ├─▶ The build backend returned an error
  ╰─▶ Call to `uv_build.build_wheel` failed (exit status: 1)

hint: Build failures usually indicate a problem with the package or the build environment
```
Here, we imagine that `thing.bin` is a binary data resource used by the code at runtime. `uv-build` seems to treat it as if it were a license file, suggesting that the glob in `license-files` is not being correctly processed — it should only match the vendored license file. (It would of course be catastrophic to try to force UTF-8 encoding onto such a file.)

It's perhaps expected that `thing.bin` wouldn't end up in the wheel built by uv-build by default, but adding a `[tool.uv.build-backend]` table with a `data` key doesn't solve the problem. (And would also not be workable in general; many real-world projects don't leverage `importlib.resources` and expect to find their data at paths relative to the source code, so redirecting them to the wheel's `.data` directory would also be disruptive.) 

Removing `**` from the glob *does* suppress the error; but then `thing.bin` remains in the wheel in its current location and so does the vendor license (in addition to being added to the `.dist-info/licenses`).

### Platform

Linux Mint 22.3 (Linux 6.8.0-146-generic x86_64 GNU/Linux)

### Version

uv 0.11.25 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)

### Python version

Python 3.12.3
title: license-file globs find non-license files and complain about encoding
